items.goal: Add GET /api/catalog/items/{id}/brand-mates (API versions 1.0 and 2.0, anonymous) to Catalog.API and a 'More from {brand}' section on the WebApp product page that lists the items it returns as catalog product cards, hidden when the list is empty. The default scenario has no brand with a single item: to check the hidden case, the verifier finds or creates (via the API or database) a brand with exactly one item.
items.modelReason: A routine endpoint and Razor section that follow the existing patterns closely.
items.verifyReason: Changes the product page; the section must be seen rendered and hidden.

items.reason: GetBrandMates shares the try block with GetCatalogItem, so a failure of the secondary brand-mates call (5xx, or a 404 from a concurrent delete) breaks the whole product page or shows it as not found.
items.fix: Wrap the GetBrandMates call in its own try/catch for HttpRequestException and fall back to an empty list so the rest of the page is unaffected.

items.title: Default count returns the four first other items by name, excluding the item itself
covers: Outputs: other items of the same brand, never the item itself
items.reason: AC1 is the core rule: same brand, exclusion of the item, name ordering and default limit. Item 203 sits inside the first four by name, so a missing exclusion would show up. Functional layer: pure API contract against the real database; the call is anonymous, which also covers the anonymous-read requirement.

items.title: count=12 returns all six other items in ordinal name order
items.reason: AC2 and the upper valid boundary of `count`. The lowercase "zulu tent" checks that ordering is ordinal (uppercase before lowercase) as the story states, not culture-aware. Functional layer, real Postgres.

items.title: count=1 returns only the first other item by name
items.reason: Lower valid boundary of `count` (just inside the limit) and proof that a count below the default is honored. Separate from case 01, which checks the default.

items.title: Only item of its brand returns 200 with an empty array
covers: Outputs: an empty array when the brand has no other items
items.reason: AC3: an empty brand-mate set must be `200` with `[]`, not 404 or null; the product page relies on it to hide the section. Functional layer.

items.title: Fewer mates than the default count returns all of them
items.reason: Distinguishes "at most count" from "exactly count": the endpoint must not pad or fail when the brand has fewer than four other items.

items.title: Out-of-stock brand-mates are included
covers: Open Questions: out-of-stock items are included
items.reason: The story's answered open question says stock is not part of the rule. Item 202 has AvailableStock 0 and would disappear if a stock filter were applied. Separate case because it is an explicit decision.

items.title: Returned items have the same shape as the single-item endpoint
covers: Outputs: the same item shape as GET /api/catalog/items/{id}
items.reason: The story requires the same item shape so clients can reuse their model. Comparing against the single-item response catches renamed or missing fields.

items.title: The endpoint is available and equivalent in API version 2.0
covers: Inputs: anonymous like the other catalog reads
items.reason: The story says the endpoint exists in both API versions. A mapping on only one version group would break clients of the other. Functional layer because versioning is an API routing concern.

items.title: Unknown item id returns 404
covers: Outputs: 404 Not Found when no item has that id
items.reason: AC4: the item lookup must fail with 404, not an empty array, so clients can tell a missing item from a brand with no mates.

items.title: count=0 is rejected with 400 problem details
items.reason: AC5 lower boundary, just outside the limit. TC-CAT-1-03 covers count=1 just inside.

items.title: count=13 is rejected with 400 problem details
items.reason: AC5 upper boundary, just outside the limit. TC-CAT-1-02 covers count=12 just inside.

items.title: Negative count is rejected with 400
items.reason: The range rule is "1 to 12", so any negative value is below 1. It is a different input class from 0 and could be handled differently (for example by an unsigned parse).

items.title: Anonymous shopper sees "More from Mates Co" with four cards of other items
covers: Outputs: up to four product cards (picture, name, price)
items.reason: AC6 end to end: the heading, the default count of four, the exclusion of the viewed item and the card content can only be verified in the browser through the WebApp-to-Catalog wiring. Anonymous covers the "not signed in" half of the criterion.

items.title: Following a brand-mate card opens that item's product page
covers: AC6: following a card opens that item's product page
items.reason: AC6 second half: the link target of each card. Separate from TC-CAT-1-13 because it checks navigation, not rendering.

items.title: Signed-in shopper sees the same section
covers: AC6: a shopper signed in or not
items.reason: AC6 says signed in or not. The section should not depend on identity; one case with the seeded user alice guards against an authenticated-only or anonymous-only code path.

items.title: Brand with fewer than four other items shows only those cards
covers: Outputs: up to four product cards (fewer than four available)
items.reason: "Up to four": the page must render a short list without placeholders or errors. Cheap because it reuses the page flow with the Duo brand.

items.title: Single-item brand shows no "More from" section and the rest of the page is intact
covers: Outputs: no items hides the section, heading included
items.reason: AC7: an empty result must hide the heading too, and the page must otherwise still render. Needs the browser because the risk is an orphan heading or a broken page.
